# One invitation. One yes. A movement in Singapore.

URL: https://faithdriven.sg/our-story/

Faith Driven Singapore began when a founder met Faith Driven Entrepreneur co-founder Henry Kaestner and was challenged to plant a chapter at home. This is how it happened, and who said yes along the way.

## In short

**Faith Driven Singapore** is the Singapore chapter of the global Faith Driven Entrepreneur (FDE) movement. It was started by **Prof. Aleks Farseev**, founder and CEO of the Singapore AI company SOMIN, after **Henry Kaestner**, co-founder of Faith Driven Entrepreneur, challenged him at the FDE global conference to plant a chapter in Singapore. The first Foundations session met at BLOCK71 Singapore on **14 August 2024**. Aleks was later joined by co-builders **Aidan Chan** and **Yuh Tyng Hsiao**, and the community has grown to more than 200 members.

## How did Faith Driven Singapore start?

It started with a conversation. At the Faith Driven Entrepreneur global conference, Aleks Farseev met Henry Kaestner, who co-founded the movement and, before that, co-founded the telecoms company Bandwidth. Henry did not ask Aleks to attend more events. He challenged him to **plant a chapter in Singapore**. In Aleks's own account on [farseev.com](https://farseev.com/#faith), "that single invitation became Faith Driven Singapore."

> Every chapter began with one person saying yes.
From the Faith Driven Singapore timeline, farseev.com

## Who is the founder of Faith Driven Singapore?

Aleks Farseev ("Sasha") was born and raised in Russia and came to Singapore in 2013 for a PhD in computer science at the National University of Singapore. He stayed, founded the marketing-intelligence company **SOMIN**, and became a research professor, a Forbes Technology Council columnist and a professional accordionist who founded Accordion Singapore. He is a father of three.

His faith has deep roots. He was baptised as an infant into the Russian Orthodox Church, and as an eight-year-old he prayed for a duck on a failed village hunt. Thirty seconds later, his mother walked in holding one. He tells that story in [our article on his Salt&Light interview](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/aleks-farseev-prayer-for-ducks/). In Singapore, he says, he "met God again", worshipping at City Harvest Church while staying rooted in the Orthodox tradition.

Before FDE, his company joined **DMV Redemptive Labs**, the accelerator of Digital Mission Ventures, first with Aleks as a cohort member and later as a mentor. That is where "business as mission" became a practice for him rather than a phrase. It also shaped his idea of [redemptive marketing](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/redemptive-marketing/).

## Why did it take time to find co-founders?

After the invitation, Aleks looked hard for a co-founder. Plenty of experienced, willing people stepped forward, but none was the right fit, and he refused to settle. The goal was specific: **a genuine community of Christ-following founders, not a business fellowship where everyone quietly sells to everyone else.**

The right people came through the sessions themselves. **Aidan Chan**, a former startup founder and venture investor, kept turning up and later led sessions himself. **Yuh Tyng Hsiao**, a marketer turned AI-and-automation entrepreneur from City Harvest Church, joined in 2025. With both of them alongside, Faith Driven Singapore truly launched.

## Timeline: how the chapter grew

Childhood, Russia
### A prayer for ducks

An eight-year-old's prayer on a village hunt becomes the story Aleks returns to "every time I have doubts about God".

2013 onwards
### Singapore

He comes for a PhD at NUS, stays, founds SOMIN, and meets God again at City Harvest Church.

2022–2023
### Tested

War cuts off much of the business. He refuses to abandon his team, keeps paying staff while they find new work, and restarts the company in Southeast Asia.

DMV Redemptive Labs
### Business as mission

First as a founder in the cohort, then as a mentor to other founders.

FDE global conference
### The invitation

Henry Kaestner challenges Aleks to plant a Faith Driven chapter in Singapore.

The group moves to Suntec, where rooms often held 20 to 27 people.

Jan–Aug 2026
### Cohort 3

A mobile community: Browzwear, Marina One, Kampung Siglap, Father's House and the YMCA.

Beyond Singapore
### Taipei, then London and Kenya

The first overseas group starts in Taipei. New groups are taking shape at Meta's London office and in Kenya.

23 Sep 2026
### FDE 2026 Conference watch party

Singapore gathers at 105 Sunset Way to watch the global conference together.

## Why does the chapter keep changing venues?

"We keep changing venues — not because we want to, but because God does," Aleks says. In two years the group met in seven places across Singapore: a startup hub, a convention centre, a tech company's office, a condominium dining room, a community retreat centre, a ministry space and the YMCA. Each was a neutral space that belonged to no single church, which suits a room of people from many churches, some from none, and at least 16 countries. You can see every session on our [gatherings page](https://faithdriven.sg/gatherings/).

## The people who said yes

### Henry Kaestner

Co-founder, Faith Driven Entrepreneur. He issued the invitation to plant a Singapore chapter.

### Aleks Farseev

Founder, Faith Driven Singapore. APAC / Southeast Asia Ambassador for Faith Driven Entrepreneur. Founder and CEO of SOMIN.

### Aidan Chan

Co-builder, Faith Driven Singapore. A former startup founder and venture investor who has led Foundations sessions.

### Yuh Tyng Hsiao

Co-builder, Faith Driven Singapore. A marketer turned entrepreneur in AI solutions, automation and digital marketing.

## What does "no cost, no catch" mean?

Gatherings and Foundations Groups are free. Volunteers run them, and monthly partners fund the food and venues. Nobody pays to belong, and nobody is there to sell. That was the higher bar Aleks set from the start, and it is still the test for every new group.

## Questions about our story

**Q: Who founded Faith Driven Singapore?**

Prof. Aleks Farseev, founder and CEO of SOMIN, started Faith Driven Singapore after Faith Driven Entrepreneur co-founder Henry Kaestner challenged him to plant a chapter in Singapore. Aidan Chan and Yuh Tyng Hsiao later joined as co-builders.

**Q: When did Faith Driven Singapore start?**

The first Foundations Group session, "Our Call to Create", met at BLOCK71 Singapore on 14 August 2024. Three cohorts have run since then.

**Q: Is Faith Driven Singapore part of Faith Driven Entrepreneur?**

Yes. It is the local Singapore chapter of the global Faith Driven Entrepreneur movement and uses FDE's Foundation Course and resources.

**Q: Does Faith Driven Singapore have groups outside Singapore?**

The Singapore team helped start the first overseas group in Taipei. New groups are forming in London and Kenya.

# What Singapore's builders say when they talk about their calling.

URL: https://faithdriven.sg/voices/

Twenty-two recorded Foundations sessions, three cohorts and 776 coded sharings. Here is what founders in Singapore actually said, in their own words, with a link to each moment in the recordings.

**22**recorded Foundations sessions, Aug 2024 – Aug 2026
**~36**hours of conversation
**776**live sharings, transcribed and coded
**16+**countries of origin in the room
**7**venues across the island
**47**people who came back again and again

## The short version

- Calling comes first. Calling and vocation is the most common theme among participants (187 of 550 participant sharings).

- Discernment matters more than prosperity. Hearing God in business decisions came up 127 times. Explicit prosperity talk came up only 19 times, and pushback against it slightly outnumbered support.

- The unicorn myth hurts. Founders spoke openly about burnout, depression and the pressure to "10x or die", and about finding an identity apart from success.

- Faith pushes back on some Asian scripts and makes room for others. The room consistently rejected shame-of-failure and "money is success" scripts. It found gentle, character-first ways to witness among Muslim, Hindu, Buddhist and secular colleagues.

- Community is the point. "Entrepreneurs struggle a lot… that's why the community is very important."

## What themes come up most?

Every live sharing from participants was coded against a fixed list of 20 themes. The facilitator's voice is counted separately and left out here. These are the eight most common themes in participant sharings:

Calling & vocation**187**
Spirit guidance & prayer**127**
Wealth & stewardship**110**
Identity & success**105**
Ethics & excellence**99**
Singapore / Asian context**97**
Community & loneliness**95**
Suffering & mental health**79**

Prosperity & blessing appeared in just 19 sharings, the second-least common theme.

## 1. Hearing God in business decisions

> Holy Spirit is my partner in this business… I just close my laptop and I say, okay, till You speak I will not do anything. And then He speaks… I'm not usually successful in the eyes of the world, but I'm so much at peace it's ridiculous.
A founder · Cohort 1, Session 7 "Ministry in Deed" · [watch at 87:14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jeSK7lAcBAU&t=5234s)

> We always go before God. We run faster than God… we want to achieve things faster, but we never check with God.
A property investor of 20+ years · Cohort 3, Session 4 "Excellence Matters" · [watch at 62:21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ninj5Pg2sDY&t=3741s)

> Over the last ten years that we have run an agency, there are at least three distinct points where God really came in with a client out of nowhere… every day we are living by grace.
Co-founder of a performance-marketing agency · Cohort 1, Session 2 "God Owns My Business" · [watch at 69:09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KUrWalKWWiY&t=4149s)

## 2. The unicorn myth and the cost of hustle

> It's always "be a unicorn, be a unicorn". VCs coming to you: you better 100x, or at least 10x… hustle, hustle. It led to that burnout.
A former tech founder and venture investor · Cohort 1, Session 3 "Don't Worship Work" · [watch at 46:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HPu4PaqkOwk&t=2815s)

> God has not left His throne. God has not lost His power. God is no less God because my business has cratered.
A startup mentor of 17 years · Cohort 1, Session 3 · [watch at 58:27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HPu4PaqkOwk&t=3507s)

> I used to run an organisation of about 4.6 billion euros… When I came back at 40 and started my company, every decision I made was wrong. Very wrong… I pray a lot. Until today I'm still praying.
Owner of a lighting manufacturer · Cohort 1, Session 6 "Ministry in Word" · [watch at 81:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0vYTBgDJLbc&t=4867s)

Read more in [Don't worship work: burnout, hustle culture and Sabbath for Asian founders](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/dont-worship-work-burnout-sabbath/).

## 3. Rest as a starting point

> The concept is not to rest from work, but rather to start working from that rest.
A founder · Cohort 3, Session 2 "God Owns My Business" · [watch at 100:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yD01eWljnTw&t=6017s)

> I've kept a Sabbath for 12 to 13 years now. It's actually the practice that has helped me accelerate.
A participant · Cohort 3, Session 2 · [watch at 95:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yD01eWljnTw&t=5752s)

## 4. Rewriting Asian scripts about success and failure

> The traditional Chinese family always thought money is probably the most important thing. Success has to be successful; there's no other alternative… More recently it's just: who am I? And what does God want me to do?
An AI-governance entrepreneur · Cohort 3, Session 5 "Faithful vs. Willful" · [watch at 58:41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1Z09O9_AUpk&t=3521s)

> Everybody thinks that to be a leader you must be the smartest, you must be the strongest. It's actually not true. A leader must be authentic, they must be vulnerable… And never forget God.
A participant · Cohort 3, Session 6 "Ministry in Word" · [watch at 85:41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wDscRK9xaSQ&t=5141s)

> Especially in Singapore, if you are not aiming for a corporate job, you tend to be looked down upon… Then Jesus showed up in my life: "I created you for a reason."
A digital creative studio founder · Cohort 1, Session 1 "Our Call to Create" · [watch at 113:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bbbIEVZ7dmw&t=6832s)

## 5. Faith at work in a multi-faith city

> I said, there's only one other thing I can do to help you have a successful outcome to the pitch: can I pray for you? Sometimes they'd say, "I'm not a Christian." I said, can I pray for you anyway?… I did it as an outflow of doing things well.
A startup mentor · Cohort 1, Session 1 · [watch at 90:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bbbIEVZ7dmw&t=5422s)

> They are Muslim… they never heard who is Moses, Abraham. So I cannot go deeper… I can tell a story. Hopefully they are harvested by other people.
A deal introducer · Cohort 3, Session 6 · [watch at 93:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wDscRK9xaSQ&t=5590s)

> Your character is a reflection of who God is. I would prefer if people come to you and say: why are you like this? How come you have so much hope?
A digital creative studio founder · Cohort 1, Session 1 · [watch at 117:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bbbIEVZ7dmw&t=7039s)

## 6. Integrity you can open the books on

> I have nothing to hide. I tell you what it is. If you'd like to do business with me, then we're the right fit. If not, thank you very much.
A business owner · Cohort 3, Session 7 "Ministry in Deed" · [watch at 61:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cTjw_5SGiiI&t=3699s)

> The problem is the same… but how you address it, from what perspective you look at it, as a believer and a non-believer, is very different. We need to have a serving heart.
A clinic co-founder · Cohort 3, Session 1 "Our Call to Create" · [watch at 95:49](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hmq7PztBWMA&t=5749s)

## 7. Why the room matters

> The running joke: you want to be closer to God, be an entrepreneur. Every day you'll be praying for something… Entrepreneurs struggle a lot, it's very easy to give up, very easy to lose focus, and that's why the community is very important.
An entrepreneur · Cohort 3, Session 5 · [watch at 70:26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1Z09O9_AUpk&t=4226s)

> Vietnam is a very persecuted church. We get shut down by the police a lot. So seeing this happen is a real blessing and grace.
A founder visiting from Da Nang, Vietnam · Cohort 3, Session 3 "Don't Worship Work" · [watch at 16:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mGUM0Li2be0&t=1010s)

## How we gathered these voices

All 22 recorded sessions on the Faith Driven Singapore YouTube channel were transcribed the same way. Each live sharing was then coded by question, theme and signal, and checked against its transcript. Curriculum films are excluded, and the facilitator's voice is counted separately from participants'. Quotes are lightly edited for readability, with filler words removed and omissions marked "…". Speakers are described by role, not by name. Transcripts come from speech recognition, so the recording is always the final word. Follow the links to hear each person say it.

Want the analysis? Read [7 insights from 22 Foundations sessions](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/what-singapore-founders-say/).

## Questions about this research

**Q: What do Christian entrepreneurs in Singapore talk about most?**

In 550 coded participant sharings from Faith Driven Singapore sessions, the most common themes were calling and vocation (187), Spirit guidance and prayer (127), wealth and stewardship (110), and identity apart from success (105).

**Q: Do faith-driven founders in Singapore believe in the prosperity gospel?**

Rarely, in these rooms. Explicit prosperity talk appeared in only 19 of 550 participant sharings, and pushback against it slightly outnumbered support. The emphasis was on discernment, meaning hearing God in business decisions, rather than on blessing.

**Q: Where can I watch the sessions?**

Every recorded session is on the Faith Driven Singapore YouTube channel. Each quote on this page links straight to its moment in the video, and the [gatherings page](https://faithdriven.sg/gatherings/) lists every session.

# Twenty-two sessions. Seven venues. One community.

URL: https://faithdriven.sg/gatherings/

Since August 2024 Faith Driven Singapore has met monthly to work through the eight sessions of the Faith Driven Entrepreneur Foundation Course. Here is every session, where it met and where to watch it.

## How it works

A **Foundations Group** is an eight-session journey through the Faith Driven Entrepreneur Foundation Course. In Singapore we meet **once a month on a Wednesday evening**, so one cohort takes about eight months. Each evening has worship, a short FDE film about a founder, teaching, and honest table discussion. The gatherings are free. You can join at any session, and you don't need to come with a group.

## What happens at a session?

- Arrive and eat. Food is on the table, thanks to our monthly partners.

- Introductions. Your life path, your path to God, what you are building and one fun fact.

- Worship. A song or two, often led by someone from the room.

- The film. A founder story and teaching from the Foundation Course.

- Discussion. Three or four questions from the course guide, answered honestly.

- Prayer. For each other's businesses, families and next steps.

## The eight sessions

Each session follows one of the "marks" of a Faith Driven Entrepreneur. The [full guide to the eight sessions](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/foundation-course-8-sessions-explained/) covers them in detail.

- Our Call to Create: work as worship, and entrepreneurship as a calling.

- God Owns My Business: stewardship over ownership.

- Don't Worship Work: identity, burnout and Sabbath.

- Excellence Matters: doing good work as witness.

- Faithful vs. Willful: roles, priorities and surrender.

- Ministry in Word: talking about faith at work.

- Ministry in Deed: loving your neighbour through business.

- Global Movement: joining what God is doing worldwide.

## Every recorded session

## Where we have gathered

BLOCK71 Singapore (Aug 2024 – Apr 2025) · Suntec Singapore (May – Nov 2025) · Browzwear (Jan – Feb 2026) · Marina One Residence (Mar – Apr 2026) · Kampung Siglap (May 2026) · Father's House (Jun and Aug 2026) · YMCA of Singapore (Jul 2026). On **23 September 2026** we met at 105 Sunset Way for the **FDE 2026 Conference watch party**. The [conference sessions are now available on demand](https://faithdrivenentrepreneur.org/2026-fde-conference/).

## Questions about gatherings

**Q: When does Faith Driven Singapore meet?**

Foundations sessions usually meet on a Wednesday evening once a month. Check the next date and venue on [Eventbrite](https://share.somin.ai/event-fde) or in the WhatsApp community.

**Q: Can I join halfway through a cohort?**

Yes. Each session stands on its own, so you can join at any point and pick up the sessions you missed in the next cohort or on YouTube.

**Q: Do I need to be a Christian to attend?**

The gatherings are designed for Christ-following entrepreneurs, but seekers and people of other faiths have joined us and are welcome.

**Q: Are the sessions recorded?**

Most are. Recordings go on the Faith Driven Singapore YouTube channel. Two sessions of Cohort 2 were not recorded.

# What is Faith Driven Entrepreneur (FDE)?

URL: https://faithdriven.sg/articles/what-is-faith-driven-entrepreneur/
Published: 2026-09-24 · Category: FDE basics

A plain-English guide to the global movement for Christ-following founders, and what it looks like here in Singapore.

## Quick answer

**Faith Driven Entrepreneur (FDE)** is a global, non-profit movement that helps Christ-following entrepreneurs who lead teams to find their community, understand God's love for them, and follow their God-given call to create. It offers a free eight-session **Foundation Course**, a book, a weekly podcast, an annual conference and local groups in cities around the world. **Faith Driven Singapore** is its Singapore chapter.

## What does Faith Driven Entrepreneur mean?

The phrase describes a founder whose faith in Jesus shapes how they build: why they start, how they treat people, how they handle money and failure, and what they count as success. FDE's own mission statement puts it this way: "To help Christ-following entrepreneurs (that lead teams) to find their community, understand God's love for them, and their God-given call to create."

The central idea is that **entrepreneurship is a calling, not a lesser, "secular" job**. Creating a business that brings order out of chaos, solves problems and gives people dignified work is a way of reflecting a creative God. FDE calls this the call to create, and it is the subject of the first session of the Foundation Course.

## Who started Faith Driven Entrepreneur?

FDE is part of the Faith Driven Movements, which also include [Faith Driven Investor](https://faithdriveninvestor.org/). **Henry Kaestner** is a co-founder. He co-founded the telecoms company Bandwidth (NASDAQ: BAND), which grew from nothing to more than US$600 million in revenue, and is a co-founder and partner at **Sovereign's Capital**, which invests in faith-driven founders in the United States and Southeast Asia. The movement's weekly podcast is hosted by Henry with co-hosts including William Norvell and Justin Forman.

## Why does FDE exist? The "99.7%" problem

In the book Faith Driven Entrepreneur, the authors estimate that there are about **582 million entrepreneurs** in the world and that roughly **180 million** of them follow Christ. Very few of those believers are in any community built for their situation. Hence the line on our home page: 99.7% are building alone. Pastors often don't speak the language of payroll and term sheets, and founder networks rarely make room for prayer. FDE exists to close that gap.

FDE also argues that business owners are unusually trusted. Its mission page cites research that business leaders are "9x more trusted than politicians" and "2x more trusted than the church". That trust gives founders an unusual platform for good.

## What does FDE offer?

- The Foundation Course. Eight free video sessions, one a week or one a month, for groups of about 10 to 15 founders. FDE says more than 30,000 entrepreneurs from over 130 countries have taken it. See [the eight sessions explained](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/foundation-course-8-sessions-explained/).

- The book. Faith Driven Entrepreneur: What It Takes to Step Into Your Purpose and Pursue Your God-Given Call to Create, by Henry Kaestner, J.D. Greear and Chip Ingram, with a foreword by Lecrae (Tyndale Momentum, 2021). Registered groups get it free.

- The podcast. Weekly conversations with founders. Asian guests include Grab's Anthony Tan and New Taipei Kings owner Phil Chen.

- The conference. A global livestream watched in local watch parties. The 2026 conference streamed on 18 September 2026, and Singapore watched it together on 23 September.

- Local groups and chapters in cities worldwide, including [Faith Driven Singapore](https://faithdriven.sg/).

## Is FDE a church, a network or an accelerator?

None of those, exactly. FDE is not a church and doesn't replace one. In Singapore, members come from City Harvest, New Creation, Kingdomcity, Methodist, Lutheran, Catholic, Orthodox and independent or house churches. It is not a sales network either: our founding principle is "a genuine community of Christ-following founders, not a business fellowship where everyone quietly sells to everyone else". And it is not an accelerator, though many members have been through accelerators such as DMV Redemptive Labs or Praxis. It is best understood as a **peer community built around a shared curriculum**.

## What does FDE look like in Singapore?

Faith Driven Singapore began on 14 August 2024 at BLOCK71 Singapore. Its founder, Aleks Farseev, had been challenged by Henry Kaestner to plant a chapter ([read the story](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/faith-driven-singapore-founding-story/)). Since then, three cohorts have worked through the Foundation Course across seven venues, with 22 sessions recorded and posted on YouTube. The chapter has grown to more than 200 members, and it helped start a group in Taipei.

[Video: Faith Driven Singapore · Session 1: Our Call to Create (Cohort 3, Browzwear)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hmq7PztBWMA)

What do people talk about in those rooms? Mostly calling, discernment and identity, not prosperity. Read [7 insights from 22 sessions](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/what-singapore-founders-say/) or browse the [voices from the room](https://faithdriven.sg/voices/).

## How do I join Faith Driven Entrepreneur in Singapore?

- Message us on [WhatsApp](https://wa.me/6591227009) and we'll suggest a next step.

- Join the [WhatsApp community](https://chat.whatsapp.com/EJtCAix4JwJDM1nmpd4XhM) for dates and prayer.

- [Register with FDE](https://share.somin.ai/fde) so the global movement can connect you.

- Come to the [next gathering](https://share.somin.ai/event-fde). It's free.

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: What is Faith Driven Entrepreneur?**

Faith Driven Entrepreneur (FDE) is a global non-profit movement that helps Christ-following entrepreneurs find community and pursue their God-given call to create, through a free Foundation Course, a book, a podcast, a conference and local groups.

**Q: Who founded Faith Driven Entrepreneur?**

Henry Kaestner, co-founder of Bandwidth and Sovereign's Capital, is a co-founder of Faith Driven Entrepreneur and of its sister movement Faith Driven Investor.

**Q: Is Faith Driven Entrepreneur free?**

Yes. The Foundation Course is free, and in Singapore the gatherings and Foundations Groups are free as well. Volunteers and monthly partners sustain them.

**Q: Is there a Faith Driven Entrepreneur group in Singapore?**

Yes. Faith Driven Singapore is the local chapter. It has met monthly since August 2024 and runs Foundations Groups across Singapore.

**Q: Do I need to lead a team to join?**

FDE is designed for entrepreneurs who lead teams, but in Singapore we welcome aspiring founders, solo builders and business leaders at every stage.

# How Faith Driven Singapore began: one invitation, one yes

URL: https://faithdriven.sg/articles/faith-driven-singapore-founding-story/
Published: 2026-09-24 · Category: Singapore chapter

A conversation with Henry Kaestner, a long search for the right co-founders, and a first session at BLOCK71. The origin of Singapore's Faith Driven Entrepreneur chapter.

## Quick answer

Faith Driven Singapore was founded by **Prof. Aleks Farseev**, CEO of the Singapore AI company SOMIN. At the Faith Driven Entrepreneur global conference he met FDE co-founder **Henry Kaestner**, who challenged him to plant a chapter in Singapore. Aleks searched for co-founders, refused to settle for the wrong fit, and launched the first Foundations Group at **BLOCK71 Singapore on 14 August 2024**. Co-builders **Aidan Chan** and **Yuh Tyng Hsiao** later joined him. The chapter now has more than 200 members and has seeded a group in Taipei.

## The meeting that started it

Henry Kaestner is used to starting things. He co-founded Bandwidth, co-founded the venture firm Sovereign's Capital, and co-founded Faith Driven Entrepreneur and Faith Driven Investor. When he met Aleks Farseev at the FDE global conference, he didn't just offer encouragement. He **challenged Aleks to plant a chapter in Singapore**.

Aleks recounts the moment on his personal site, [farseev.com](https://farseev.com/#faith): "At the Faith Driven Entrepreneur global conference, Aleks met co-founder Henry Kaestner — who challenged him to plant a chapter in Singapore. That single invitation became Faith Driven Singapore."

## Why Aleks was ready to say yes

The invitation landed on prepared ground. Aleks grew up in the Russian Orthodox tradition. As a boy he saw a prayer for a duck answered within 30 seconds, and he still calls it the memory he returns to "every time I have doubts about God" ([the full story](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/aleks-farseev-prayer-for-ducks/)). He came to Singapore in 2013 for a PhD at NUS, founded SOMIN, and "met God again" worshipping at City Harvest Church.

Then came the hardest stretch of his working life. When war broke out, much of SOMIN's team and business were in Russia. Salt&Light reported that the company was losing more than $150,000 a month to keep supporting staff while they found new jobs. Aleks refused to abandon them. He even flew back into conscription risk to secure a research grant that paid SOMIN's people. The company restarted in Southeast Asia and joined **DMV Redemptive Labs**, the accelerator of Digital Mission Ventures. There, "business as mission" stopped being a phrase and became a practice. Aleks was a founder in the cohort first, and later a mentor.

## The long search for co-founders

An invitation is not a community. Aleks looked hard for a co-founder. According to farseev.com, "plenty of experienced, willing people stepped forward — yet none was the right fit, and he refused to settle."

The bar was specific. He wanted **"a genuine community of Christ-following founders, not a business fellowship where everyone quietly sells to everyone else."** Many business fellowships drift into lead generation. Faith Driven Singapore would be free, with no cost and no catch, and centred on the FDE Foundation Course rather than on networking.

## Session 1 at BLOCK71

So he started anyway. On **Wednesday 14 August 2024**, the first Foundation Study met at BLOCK71 Singapore, the startup hub at 71 Ayer Rajah Crescent. It was billed as "a group in Singapore meeting monthly at Block71", and SOMIN was listed as the organiser. The recording of that first night shows a room of 19 voices: a startup mentor of 17 years, a tax professional turned XR founder, a pastor's kid running a digital studio, an e-commerce seller and a self-described free-thinker, all answering the same question: tell us your life path and your path to God.

[Video: Faith Driven Singapore · Cohort 1, Session 1: Our Call to Create (BLOCK71, Aug 2024)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bbbIEVZ7dmw)

Aleks told the room he was leading worship for the first time in his life. His Orthodox tradition doesn't have congregational singing, so this was new to him.

## The people who said yes

The co-founders came from inside the sessions. **Aidan Chan**, a former startup founder and venture investor, kept coming back across all three cohorts and eventually led sessions himself. **Yuh Tyng Hsiao**, born in Taiwan and raised in Singapore, is a marketer turned AI-and-automation entrepreneur from City Harvest Church who joined in 2025. With both of them alongside, the chapter "truly launched".

## A community on the move

Over two years the group met in seven venues: BLOCK71, Suntec, Browzwear's office, a condominium dining room at Marina One, Kampung Siglap, Father's House and the YMCA. "We keep changing venues — not because we want to, but because God does," Aleks says. Across cohorts, 47 people came back more than once, 24 followed the group to more than one venue, and 16 crossed from one cohort to the next.

## From Singapore to Taipei, London and Kenya

Founders and investors from Taiwan have visited Singapore sessions, and the chapter's first overseas group has since started in Taipei. "FDE has been going great in TW btw! Thank you for introducing :)", Angie from Taipei wrote back. New groups are now forming at Meta's London office and in Kenya. Aleks serves as an **APAC / Southeast Asia Ambassador** for Faith Driven Entrepreneur.

## What the founding story teaches

- Movements start with a specific ask. Henry didn't say "get involved". He said "plant a chapter".

- Protect the culture before you scale. Refusing the wrong co-founder cost time and kept the community honest.

- Start before it's perfect. The right co-builders turned up in the room once the room existed.

- Every chapter begins with one person saying yes.

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: Who started Faith Driven Entrepreneur in Singapore?**

Prof. Aleks Farseev, founder and CEO of SOMIN, started Faith Driven Singapore after Faith Driven Entrepreneur co-founder Henry Kaestner challenged him to plant a chapter. Aidan Chan and Yuh Tyng Hsiao are co-builders.

**Q: When was the first Faith Driven Singapore session?**

Wednesday 14 August 2024, at BLOCK71 Singapore, with Session 1 "Our Call to Create" of the Foundation Course.

**Q: How did Henry Kaestner meet the Singapore founder?**

They met at the Faith Driven Entrepreneur global conference, where Henry challenged Aleks to plant a Faith Driven chapter in Singapore.

**Q: How big is Faith Driven Singapore?**

The community has grown to more than 200 members. Three cohorts have completed 22 recorded Foundations sessions, and a group has started in Taipei.

# A child's prayer for ducks and the faith behind an AI start-up

URL: https://faithdriven.sg/articles/aleks-farseev-prayer-for-ducks/
Published: 2026-09-24 · Category: Founder stories

What Salt&Light's 2024 profile of Aleks Farseev tells us about faith, fear and building a company through a war, and why he still tells the duck story.

## Quick answer

In February 2024, the Singapore Christian news site **Salt&Light** profiled **Prof. Aleks Farseev**, co-founder and CEO of the AI marketing company **SOMIN** and later the founder of Faith Driven Singapore. The article traces his faith to an answered prayer at eight years old, when a wild duck ended up in his mother's hands 30 seconds after he prayed on a failed hunt. It follows that faith through a frightening trip to Russia during conscription and a war that forced his company to restart in Southeast Asia. Its thesis is simple: "Every time I have doubts about God, I remember this incident."

## What happened with the ducks?

As a boy, Aleks spent summers at his grandmother's village in Russia. He played the accordion, and the grown-ups brought him along on duck hunts "to provide musical entertainment". One day the men came back empty-handed. Aleks, "all of eight years old", offered to pray. "My mother had taught me to pray for my needs," he told Salt&Light.

The men laughed. Then, "not more than 30 seconds after young Aleks finished his prayer, his mother appeared with a duck in hand." She said she had been walking through the village when the duck flew into her hand.

> I am a mathematician. I know the odds. Never before and never after have I seen wild ducks run into a person's hand in the middle of a village.
Aleks Farseev, to Salt&Light (2024)

For a founder who later built a company on statistics and machine learning, the story is less about ducks than about **where the evidence points**. Aleks grew up in a Christian home, baptised as an infant into the Russian Orthodox Church. The article notes that "70-odd years of Communism… was no match for the more than 1,000 years of Russian Orthodoxy."

## Who is Aleks Farseev?

Aleks came to Singapore in 2013 to do a PhD in computer science at the National University of Singapore, and he stayed. He founded **SOMIN** (SoMin.ai), which Salt&Light describes as "AI that mines data from social media to predict behaviour and then uses that information to create targeted digital ads". He is also a research professor, a former Forbes Technology Council columnist, a professional accordionist and a father of three. He jokes: "People think I am angry all the time but it's just my face."

## The Screwtape Letters and a flight into fear

The article's most gripping section comes from around 2023. A research-grant issue forced Aleks to fly back to Russia, where men were being conscripted, to secure funds that paid SOMIN's staff. "All my relatives in Russia told me not to come."

On a stopover in London he attended a Russian Orthodox service and, in the church bookshop, unexpectedly found C.S. Lewis's The Screwtape Letters. He then went to Holy Trinity Brompton, where the vicar told him: "God already told you what to do. You already know. You don't need to ask anymore."

On the flight, "one of the strongest fears in my life", he read the passage in which the senior devil tells the junior one never to let the man realise that all the bad things cannot happen to him at once. The two-week trip passed without incident and the grant was secured. "I am not a very sensitive person," Aleks said. "So God talks to me in a straightforward fashion."

## Building through a war

When war broke out, many of SOMIN's employees and much of its business were in Russia. The company was "haemorrhaging as much as over $150,000 a month", sustaining staff and giving them time to find other jobs, and it had to start again in a new market, Southeast Asia. Aleks sees providence even in the timing: "He let us fund raise just before the war broke out. So we had enough cash to go through those two years."

> I never asked God why this happened. Just listen to what He wants you to do.
Aleks Farseev, to Salt&Light

That redirection led SOMIN into **DMV Redemptive Labs**, the accelerator of Digital Mission Ventures for "early-stage tech founders looking to use their business for Kingdom impact". Later, it led to a conversation with Henry Kaestner and to [the founding of Faith Driven Singapore](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/faith-driven-singapore-founding-story/).

## Faith in the business model

The profile ends on ethics. SOMIN is "very selective" about industries such as gambling. It "often compromise[s] margins to help businesses who really want to change for better", and sometimes tells a client: "You don't need our services, use the money to invest in infrastructure to improve." Aleks wants SOMIN "to redeem the advertising world", an industry where he says turnover is the second-highest of any sector. That conviction later became his idea of [redemptive marketing](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/redemptive-marketing/).

On AI, he is calm: "AI is just Math with powerful computers." And: "Everything can be used by God in a good way, just as it can be used by the devil in a bad way."

## Lessons for founders

- Keep a memorial stone. Aleks goes back to one undeniable answer to prayer whenever doubt returns.

- Peace doesn't depend on the deal. When a $500,000 contract was cancelled at the last moment, he described "a great sense of peace", "one more chance for me to be reminded that God is in control".

- Pray the uncomfortable prayer. He quotes a pastor: "God, don't give me what I don't need even if I want it or ask for it. I think this part is very important for start-ups."

- Trouble is training. "In this world, it is impossible to be without tribulations. But that is the only thing that sharpens us for assignments in the future."

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: What is the "prayer for ducks" story?**

At eight years old, on a failed duck hunt in his grandmother's Russian village, Aleks Farseev prayed for a duck. About 30 seconds later his mother appeared holding one that had flown into her hand. He says he remembers it every time he doubts God.

**Q: Who is Aleks Farseev?**

Aleks Farseev is a Russian-born, Singapore-based AI entrepreneur and professor. He is the founder and CEO of SOMIN, founder of Faith Driven Singapore, and an APAC / Southeast Asia Ambassador for Faith Driven Entrepreneur.

**Q: Where was the Salt&Light article published?**

On saltandlight.sg on 20 February 2024, under the title "How a child-like prayer for ducks laid the faith foundation for an AI start-up", by Christine Leow.

## Sources

- [Christine Leow, "How a child-like prayer for ducks laid the faith foundation for an AI start-up", Salt&Light, 20 Feb 2024](https://saltandlight.sg/business/how-a-child-like-prayer-for-ducks-laid-the-faith-foundation-for-an-ai-start-up/)

- [farseev.com — Faith: the journey](https://farseev.com/#faith)

# What is redemptive marketing?

URL: https://faithdriven.sg/articles/redemptive-marketing/
Published: 2026-09-24 · Category: Faith at work

A faith-driven answer to digital advertising's transparency and performance problem, from a Forbes Technology Council article by the founder of Faith Driven Singapore.

## Quick answer

**Redemptive marketing** applies redemptive entrepreneurship to advertising. It means measuring success by the client's real business outcomes rather than by easy vanity metrics, being transparent about what campaigns actually achieve, being willing to sacrifice short-term margin for a client's long-term good, and using technology such as AI so that marketers "no longer need to fabricate results". Aleks Farseev set out the argument in a May 2024 **Forbes Technology Council** article. It sums up with: "sometimes you need to sacrifice for your partner or client to benefit from the work you do, with the ultimate faith that this will lead to a long, genuine partnership."

## Where does the term come from?

"Redemptive entrepreneurship" is a phrase used across the faith-and-business world, including by accelerators such as Praxis and DMV Redemptive Labs. It describes businesses that aim to leave people, industries and places better than they found them. Aleks Farseev, founder of SOMIN and of [Faith Driven Singapore](https://faithdriven.sg/), took that idea into his own industry in the Forbes article "[Redemptive Marketing: The Path To Resolving Transparency And Performance Dilemmas In Digital Advertising](https://www.forbes.com/councils/forbestechcouncil/2024/05/20/redemptive-marketing-the-path-to-resolving-transparency-and-performance-dilemmas-in-digital-advertising/)" (20 May 2024). He wrote it "as the member leader of the Forbes Technology Council Marketing and Advertising Group and a faith-driven entrepreneur".

## What problem is redemptive marketing trying to fix?

Aleks surveyed more than 100 business owners around the world. The findings:

- 40% of marketers were dissatisfied with performance.

- 28% of digital advertisers struggled to determine the actual impact of their campaigns.

- Transparency was the top concern.

His diagnosis starts with history. Agencies built their model in the TV era, when media buying was "a commodity trading game". Digital platforms made direct buying transparent and reduced or dropped commissions. That left some agencies promoting "simpler, more easily achievable metrics, such as clicks". The result is "a vicious cycle, stifling innovation", in which staff "might be pressured into unethical behaviors or outright falsehoods". Digital advertising, he notes, has "the second-highest turnover rate in any industry, trailing only behind the travel sector".

His example: a Ferrari ad can rack up clicks from people who "might not be actual buyers or even have the means to purchase". The dashboard looks good, but the business gets nothing.

## The principles of redemptive marketing

- Measure what matters to the client. "True transparency requires metrics that directly correlate with business objectives", which means sales and qualified demand, not clicks.

- Tell the truth about results. Nobody should have to choose between lying and feeling bad at their job. At the first Faith Driven Singapore session Aleks put it this way: "people don't need to choose between lying and feeling that they're not good in what they do."

- Sacrifice for the partner. Sometimes the redemptive move costs you money. Salt&Light reported that SOMIN "often compromise[s] margins to help businesses who really want to change for better", and occasionally tells a client, "You don't need our services, use the money to invest in infrastructure to improve."

- Choose what you amplify. SOMIN is "very selective" about industries such as gambling. "Marketing can be a healthy industry because it brings relevant knowledge to people on what to buy and what not want to buy."

- Use technology as a coach, not a cover. AI and large language models "can now pre-evaluate ads to prevent budget waste", identify personas and draft content, so that "marketers will no longer need to fabricate results."

- Play the long game. The aim is "a long, genuine partnership with deeper and greater value", and an industry that shifts "from a culture driven by deceit and politics to one based on trust and sound decision-making".

## Why is this a faith question, not just a business one?

For Christ-following founders, redemption is the whole shape of the story: something broken is bought back and made new. Redemptive marketing treats a whole industry as something worth redeeming rather than escaping. That echoes FDE's Session 4, Excellence Matters, and Session 7, Ministry in Deed, where the question is whether your business loves its neighbours through the product, the price and the truth you tell.

It also matches what Singapore founders say in our sessions. One business owner told Cohort 3, "I have nothing to hide. I tell you what it is. If you'd like to do business with me, then we're the right fit." ([watch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cTjw_5SGiiI&t=3699s)). More in [voices from the room](https://faithdriven.sg/voices/).

## How to practise redemptive marketing: a checklist

- Agree on one business outcome per campaign, such as revenue, qualified leads or retention, before you agree on any media metric.

- Report bad weeks as clearly as good ones.

- Pre-test creative before spending, instead of "learning" on the client's budget.

- Tell a client when they shouldn't buy from you.

- Decide in advance which products and industries you won't promote.

- Build a team culture where nobody is rewarded for massaging numbers.

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: What is redemptive marketing?**

Redemptive marketing applies redemptive entrepreneurship to advertising. It means transparent, outcome-based measurement, honesty about results, a willingness to sacrifice short-term margin for the client's good, and using AI to prevent waste rather than to hide it.

**Q: Who coined redemptive marketing?**

The phrase was set out by Aleks Farseev, founder of SOMIN and Faith Driven Singapore, in a Forbes Technology Council article published on 20 May 2024. It builds on the wider idea of redemptive entrepreneurship.

**Q: How is redemptive marketing different from ethical marketing?**

Ethical marketing mostly avoids harm. Redemptive marketing also aims to restore trust in a broken system, and it accepts personal cost, such as lower margins or turned-down deals, for the sake of the client and the industry.

**Q: What role does AI play in redemptive marketing?**

In Farseev's argument, AI pre-evaluates ads to prevent budget waste and acts as a coach for marketers. Better predictions remove the pressure to inflate or fabricate results.

## Sources

- [Aleks Farseev, "Redemptive Marketing: The Path To Resolving Transparency And Performance Dilemmas In Digital Advertising", Forbes Technology Council, 20 May 2024](https://www.forbes.com/councils/forbestechcouncil/2024/05/20/redemptive-marketing-the-path-to-resolving-transparency-and-performance-dilemmas-in-digital-advertising/)

- [Salt&Light, 20 Feb 2024](https://saltandlight.sg/business/how-a-child-like-prayer-for-ducks-laid-the-faith-foundation-for-an-ai-start-up/)

- [Faith Driven Singapore, Cohort 1 Session 1 recording](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bbbIEVZ7dmw&t=1031s)

# Faith Driven Entrepreneurs in Asia

URL: https://faithdriven.sg/articles/faith-driven-entrepreneurs-in-asia/
Published: 2026-09-24 · Category: Asian FDE stories

From ride-hailing and wealth management to basketball and natural cosmetics, these are the Asian founders whose stories Faith Driven Entrepreneur tells, and where to watch them.

## Quick answer

Asia's best-known Faith Driven Entrepreneur stories include **Anthony Tan** of Grab (Southeast Asia), **Samuel Rhee** of Endowus (Singapore), **Phil Chen** of the New Taipei Kings (Taiwan), **Dylan Wilk** of Human Nature (Philippines) and **Jeremy Lin** (Taiwan/US). FDE has a dedicated **FDE Asia** podcast and website. Local groups meet in **Singapore**, **Taipei** and **Hong Kong**, among other cities.

## Why Asian stories matter

Most faith-and-business material is American. Asian founders face different pressures: family expectations about money and prestige, shame around failure, workplaces with many faiths, and in some countries real restrictions on Christian gatherings. In 550 participant sharings from Faith Driven Singapore sessions, the "Singapore / Asian context" theme came up **97 times**. People in the room need stories that sound like their own lives.

## Anthony Tan: Grab (Southeast Asia)

Grab began as an answer to women's safety in taxis and became Southeast Asia's leading super app. FDE features co-founder Anthony Tan in its "Excellence Matters" film, Serving 9 Million Entrepreneurs, and on podcast episode 131. His themes are the 4Hs (Hunger, Heart, Honour, Humility), Matthew 25:40, and protecting drivers when rides fell 90% in COVID. [Read the full story →](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/anthony-tan-grab-faith-driven-entrepreneur/)

[Video: Excellence Matters | Serving 9 Million Entrepreneurs | Anthony Tan](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DLBiq2p_Ws8)

## Samuel Rhee: Endowus (Singapore)

Endowus co-founder Samuel Rhee is the subject of the FDE profile film **I Sacrifice, We Win**. It covers a Morgan Stanley promotion he gave up, the fee-free approach to wealth management he built, and the choice between God and Mammon. Cohort 2 of Faith Driven Singapore watched it in its fifth session in August 2025, and discussed it in the room.

[Video: Faith Driven Singapore · Cohort 2, Session 5 (Endowus / Samuel Rhee film), Aug 2025](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jz_Stn_6Qqk)

## Phil Chen: New Taipei Kings (Taiwan)

A former Silicon Valley VC and ordained pastor, Phil Chen owns the New Taipei Kings, the 2025 inaugural TPBL champions. FDE's film No Out of Bounds and podcast episode 291 cover identity in Christ and his line "your attention is your worship". [Read the full story →](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/phil-chen-new-taipei-kings/)

## Dylan Wilk: Human Nature (Philippines)

Dylan Wilk made a fortune young in the UK, then moved to the Philippines and co-founded the natural-products social enterprise **Human Nature**. FDE tells his story in podcast episode 297, A Transformation from Greed to Grace, and on FDE Asia episode 29 with his wife Anna, Leaving Wealth, Discovering Purpose.

## Jeremy Lin: from the court to the cap table

The NBA champion who later played for the New Taipei Kings joined FDE podcast episode 232, From Pro Athlete to Entrepreneur (with Patricia Sun), and episode 292 on hearing from God, alongside Nicky Gumbel and Kim Avery. He also appeared on Faith Driven Investor episode 140.

## FDE Asia

Faith Driven Entrepreneur runs an Asia-focused site and the **Faith Driven Entrepreneur Asia** podcast (on Apple Podcasts and Spotify). Recent guests include Dylan and Anna Wilk, Anil David, Reuben Ang and Dr Mark Lovatt. There is also a "Best of FDE Asia" YouTube playlist. FDE's **Hong Kong** city network has its own leadership committee.

## Groups in Asia you can join

- Singapore: [Faith Driven Singapore](https://faithdriven.sg/). It has met monthly since August 2024, has 200+ members and has recorded 22 sessions.

- Taipei: the first overseas group started by the Singapore chapter.

- Hong Kong: an FDE city network that also hosted a 2026 conference watch party.

- Vietnam and beyond: founders from Da Nang have visited Singapore sessions. One of them reminded the room that "Vietnam is a very persecuted church. We get shut down by the police a lot."

## What Asian faith-driven founders have in common

- They move from face to grace. They redefine success away from family prestige and toward faithfulness.

- They serve many small entrepreneurs, whether drivers, merchants, farmers or players.

- They witness through character in multi-faith settings, earning the right to speak.

- They hold wealth loosely, from Samuel Rhee's sacrifice to Dylan Wilk's "greed to grace".

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: Is there a Faith Driven Entrepreneur Asia?**

Yes. FDE runs an Asia-focused website and the "Faith Driven Entrepreneur Asia" podcast, and local groups meet in cities including Singapore, Taipei and Hong Kong.

**Q: Which Asian founders are featured by Faith Driven Entrepreneur?**

They include Anthony Tan (Grab), Samuel Rhee (Endowus), Phil Chen (New Taipei Kings), Dylan Wilk (Human Nature) and Jeremy Lin, along with guests on the FDE Asia podcast.

**Q: Where can I watch Asian FDE stories?**

On YouTube: "Excellence Matters | Serving 9 Million Entrepreneurs | Anthony Tan" and "No Out of Bounds | Phil Chen & New Taipei Kings", plus the "Best of FDE Asia" playlist and the Faith Driven Singapore channel.

# Anthony Tan and Grab: excellence as service

URL: https://faithdriven.sg/articles/anthony-tan-grab-faith-driven-entrepreneur/
Published: 2026-09-24 · Category: Asian FDE stories

Southeast Asia's best-known start-up began with a question about who gets home safely. Here is how Faith Driven Entrepreneur tells the story of Grab's co-founder, and what founders in Singapore can take from it.

## Quick answer

**Anthony Tan**, co-founder and Group CEO of **Grab**, is one of the most prominent Asian voices in the Faith Driven Entrepreneur movement. FDE features him in the Foundation Course theme **"Excellence Matters"**, in a film titled Serving 9 Million Entrepreneurs, and on **FDE Podcast episode 131**. His story frames business as care for people: Grab began as an answer to women's safety in taxis, runs on four values (Hunger, Heart, Honour, Humility), and takes Matthew 25:40 as its guiding verse.

## Who is Anthony Tan?

Anthony Tan is Malaysian and based in Singapore. He co-founded Grab with Tan Hooi Ling after meeting her at Harvard Business School. He studied at the University of Chicago before his Harvard MBA, and FDE notes that his great-grandfather was a taxi driver. He comes from a family car business, and he chose to build something that served drivers and passengers rather than simply selling vehicles.

## How did Grab start?

According to FDE's episode notes, Grab started at Harvard Business School as an answer to a specific problem: **women's safety in taxis** in Southeast Asia. The first product was a way to book a known, trackable driver. From that narrow, human problem grew one of the region's largest technology companies. At the time of the FDE episode it had 198 million app downloads, 9 million drivers, 352 cities in 8 countries and a US$14 billion valuation.

## What does "serving 9 million entrepreneurs" mean?

The title of the FDE film changes the usual way of seeing Grab. Its drivers, delivery partners and merchants aren't just "supply". Each one is a small entrepreneur running their own tiny business. Excellence, in this view, isn't polish for its own sake. It is **building a platform good enough that millions of small business owners can feed their families through it**.

[Video: Excellence Matters | Serving 9 Million Entrepreneurs | Anthony Tan](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DLBiq2p_Ws8)

## The 4Hs: Hunger, Heart, Honour, Humility

Grab's four company values show where faith and leadership meet:

- Hunger: the drive to keep improving and to win.

- Heart: caring about the people the company serves.

- Honour: integrity, doing what you say.

- Humility: holding success loosely and staying teachable.

His guiding verse is **Matthew 25:40**: "Whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me."

## Faith under pressure: Grab in COVID-19

When the pandemic hit, ride volumes fell by around 90%. FDE recounts how Grab moved more than **150,000 drivers into delivery** and onboarded more than **80,000 merchants**, keeping income flowing to the people who depended on the platform. It is a case study in the Foundation Course's idea of ministry in deed: loving your neighbour through the way the business actually works.

## Why this story lands in Singapore

For many founders in our rooms, Grab is the local proof that a Southeast Asian company can reach global scale. Anthony Tan's story adds a harder question: whom is the scale for? That question comes up again and again in Faith Driven Singapore sessions. One founder told Cohort 3 that "the problem is the same… but how you address it, as a believer and a non-believer, is very different. We need to have a serving heart" ([watch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hmq7PztBWMA&t=5749s)).

Singapore has its own FDE film too. Endowus co-founder **Samuel Rhee**'s profile, I Sacrifice, We Win, was screened at Cohort 2's fifth session. Read more in [Faith Driven Entrepreneurs in Asia](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/faith-driven-entrepreneurs-in-asia/).

## Lessons for founders

- Start with a person, not a market. Grab started with a woman who needed to get home safely.

- Define excellence by who it serves. Nine million small entrepreneurs is a better north star than a valuation.

- Write your values down, and make humility one of them.

- In a crisis, protect the people who depend on you before you protect the metrics.

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: Is Grab's founder a Christian?**

Yes. Grab co-founder and Group CEO Anthony Tan has spoken publicly about his Christian faith, including on the Faith Driven Entrepreneur podcast (episode 131) and in FDE's "Excellence Matters" film.

**Q: What are Grab's 4Hs?**

Hunger, Heart, Honour and Humility, the four company values Anthony Tan describes as the core of Grab's culture.

**Q: Which FDE session features Anthony Tan?**

FDE's "Excellence Matters" material, which is Session 4 of the Foundation Course, features Anthony Tan in a film titled "Serving 9 Million Entrepreneurs".

# "No Out of Bounds": Phil Chen and the New Taipei Kings

URL: https://faithdriven.sg/articles/phil-chen-new-taipei-kings/
Published: 2026-09-24 · Category: Asian FDE stories

A venture capitalist, pastor and team owner on why identity comes before achievement, told through one of Taiwan's most successful basketball clubs.

## Quick answer

**Phil Chen** is the owner of the **New Taipei Kings**, a Taiwanese professional basketball team founded in 2021, and CEO of Cold Electric. He is a former Silicon Valley venture capitalist and an ordained pastor. Faith Driven Entrepreneur tells his story in the film **No Out of Bounds | Phil Chen & New Taipei Kings** and on **FDE Podcast episode 291**, where he explains how he finds his identity in Christ rather than in deals, titles or trophies.

[Video: No Out of Bounds | Phil Chen & New Taipei Kings](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ah99wdRROys)

## Who is Phil Chen?

Phil Chen's career runs across venture capital, company-building, ministry and sport. According to FDE's episode notes, he:

- worked as a venture capitalist in Silicon Valley;

- is a serial entrepreneur and CEO of Cold Electric;

- studied at Fuller Seminary, the first in his family to go to seminary, and is an ordained pastor;

- owns the New Taipei Kings.

He also describes the shame of being the first in his family to attend community college rather than a prestigious university, and how Scripture, not status, gave him confidence. It is a very Asian story about family expectation and face, retold through grace.

## Who are the New Taipei Kings?

The New Taipei Kings were founded in **2021** and play at Xinzhuang Gymnasium in New Taipei City. They competed in the P. LEAGUE+ from 2021 to 2024, winning the league title in 2024, and then joined the new TPBL. There they won the **inaugural TPBL championship on 29 June 2025**. The club is owned by Kings Blessed Investment, with Phil Chen as CEO. NBA veteran **Jeremy Lin**, himself an outspoken Christian, played for the Kings from 2023 to 2025. The club retired his number 7 in December 2025.

## "Your attention is your worship"

The line from the podcast that stays with listeners is Phil's reading of Jesus's teaching on worry in Luke: **"Your attention is your worship."** Whatever holds a founder's attention, whether the fundraise, the league table or the next deal, is what they are actually worshipping. It is the same diagnosis as FDE's Session 3, [Don't Worship Work](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/dont-worship-work-burnout-sabbath/).

Phil also draws on N.T. Wright's teaching about the kingdom of God. On that view, business and sport are not outside God's concern. Nothing is "out of bounds".

## What "no out of bounds" means for founders

In basketball, "out of bounds" is where play stops. The film's title turns that around: there is no part of life (a boardroom, a locker room, a cap table) where faith stops applying. For Asian founders who were taught to keep religion private at work, that is a direct challenge. Faith Driven Singapore's facilitator said the same thing in one session: "I found in Asia, even if you're Christian, you don't talk about it."

## Why Taiwan matters to Faith Driven Singapore

Taiwan is part of our own story. Founders and investors from Taiwan have joined Singapore sessions, co-builder Yuh Tyng Hsiao was born in Taiwan, and **the first overseas group started by the Singapore chapter meets in Taipei**. "FDE has been going great in TW btw!" one member there wrote. Phil Chen's story shows what the next generation of Taiwanese faith-driven builders could look like: global in ambition and settled in identity.

## Lessons for founders

- Audit your attention. Look at your calendar and your phone. What gets your attention is what you worship.

- Let shame be answered by Scripture, not by status.

- Build teams, on court and in the company, where people are more than their stats.

- Treat nothing as out of bounds for integrity, generosity or prayer.

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: Who owns the New Taipei Kings?**

The New Taipei Kings are owned by Kings Blessed Investment, with Phil Chen as CEO. Faith Driven Entrepreneur features Phil Chen as the team's owner in the film "No Out of Bounds".

**Q: What is "No Out of Bounds"?**

It is a Faith Driven Entrepreneur film about Phil Chen and the New Taipei Kings, exploring how faith applies to every area of business and sport. It is on YouTube.

**Q: Did Jeremy Lin play for the New Taipei Kings?**

Yes. Jeremy Lin played for the New Taipei Kings from 2023 to 2025, and the club retired his number 7 in December 2025.

**Q: Which FDE podcast episode features Phil Chen?**

Episode 291: "How a Venture Capitalist, Serial Entrepreneur, and Basketball Team Owner Finds His Identity in Christ with Phil Chen".

## Sources

- [YouTube — No Out of Bounds | Phil Chen & New Taipei Kings](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ah99wdRROys)

- [FDE Podcast Ep. 291 — Phil Chen](https://www.faithdrivenentrepreneur.org/podcast-inventory/episode-291-how-a-venture-capitalist-serial-entrepreneur-and-basketball-team-owner-finds-his-identity-in-christ-with-phil-chen)

# The Foundation Course: all eight sessions explained

URL: https://faithdriven.sg/articles/foundation-course-8-sessions-explained/
Published: 2026-09-24 · Category: FDE basics

What each session of the Faith Driven Entrepreneur Foundation Course covers, which films play, which questions get discussed, and where to watch Singapore's recorded sessions.

## Quick answer

The **Faith Driven Entrepreneur Foundation Course** is a free, eight-session video curriculum for groups of about 10 to 15 entrepreneurs. The sessions are: **1. Our Call to Create · 2. God Owns My Business · 3. Don't Worship Work · 4. Excellence Matters · 5. Faithful vs. Willful · 6. Ministry in Word · 7. Ministry in Deed · 8. Global Movement.** Each has a founder profile film, teaching (hosted by J.D. Greear in the standard edition, with introductions from Henry Kaestner) and discussion questions. FDE says more than 30,000 entrepreneurs in over 130 countries have taken it.

## How the course works

Groups usually meet weekly for eight weeks. In Singapore we meet **monthly**, so each cohort runs for about eight months, which gives busy founders time to apply each session. A typical evening includes food, introductions, worship, the film, and 45 to 60 minutes of discussion. Registered groups receive the Faith Driven Entrepreneur book free.

## Session 1: Our Call to Create

**The big idea:** God is a creator, and building a business is a way of reflecting His image. It is not second-class to "full-time ministry". The standard film profiles Dave Munson of Saddleback Leather. The discussion asks whether you need forced "Christian branding" to be a faithful founder. In Singapore, most people in the room preferred an excellence-first witness. As one mentor said: "I did it as an outflow of doing things well."

[Watch Singapore's Session 1 (Cohort 3)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hmq7PztBWMA)

## Session 2: God Owns My Business

**The big idea:** you are a steward, not an owner. The standard film features WastePlan in South Africa, and the teaching draws on 2 Corinthians 9. Cohort 3 watched a substitute episode on identity featuring Phil Vischer of VeggieTales, whose company went bankrupt. A Singapore agency founder applied the idea to parenting: "my two kids… we're really stewards of them. It's a very Chinese thing."

[Video: Faith Driven Singapore · Session 2: God Owns My Business (Cohort 3, Browzwear)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yD01eWljnTw)

## Session 3: Don't Worship Work

**The big idea:** work makes a good servant and a terrible god. The teaching goes through Ecclesiastes (Solomon's four disappointments) alongside statistics on founders' mental health. This session produced the most honest sharing in Singapore, on burnout, depression and the unicorn myth. See [our full article](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/dont-worship-work-burnout-sabbath/).

## Session 4: Excellence Matters

**The big idea:** excellent work is itself a form of worship and witness (Colossians 3:23–24). The standard film profiles Don Flow of Flow Automotive, whose dealerships use one-estimate pricing. FDE's wider "Excellence Matters" material also features Grab's [Anthony Tan](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/anthony-tan-grab-faith-driven-entrepreneur/). Cohort 3 watched the story of Dr Ngozi Onyia, founder of a hospital in Lagos: "I serve an excellent God."

## Session 5: Faithful vs. Willful

**The big idea:** faithful founders put roles in order (God, family, work) and surrender outcomes. The teaching covers Psalm 127, sleep and Matthew 6:33. Cohort 2 watched Endowus co-founder Samuel Rhee's film, I Sacrifice, We Win. One Singapore participant described leaving a joint business with her husband when she sensed God telling her to speak up.

## Session 6: Ministry in Word

**The big idea:** talking about Jesus at work, humbly and "leading with a limp" (the story of Jacob). The standard film profiles John and Ashley Marsh of the Marsh Collective. In multi-faith Singapore this session is where the room works out how far to go with Muslim, Hindu, Buddhist and secular colleagues. One participant tells Noah's story to colleagues who have never heard of Moses.

## Session 7: Ministry in Deed

**The big idea:** your business loves your neighbour through its products, prices, pay and hiring. The standard film profiles Camcraft, a precision-machining company with a corporate chaplain, open books and a practice of hiring ex-offenders. The teaching covers identity as a beloved child and Luther on "daily bread".

## Session 8: Global Movement

**The big idea:** faith-driven businesses are part of God's worldwide mission, in the 10/40 window and beyond. The standard film is NatureSweet Tomatoes and Isaiah 58: "a vision I will not see". For Singapore, this session has connected the room to groups in Taipei, Vietnam, London and Kenya.

## Tips for leading a Foundations Group in Asia

- Protect the introduction round. "Your life path and your path to God" is often the most powerful 30 minutes of the night.

- Ask which church people attend, so everyone knows the room is ecumenical.

- Use neutral venues that no single church owns.

- Record the sessions, with consent. Recordings help people who missed a session and help the movement learn.

- Keep it free and keep it free of selling.

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: What are the 8 sessions of the Faith Driven Entrepreneur Foundation Course?**

Our Call to Create; God Owns My Business; Don't Worship Work; Excellence Matters; Faithful vs. Willful; Ministry in Word; Ministry in Deed; and Global Movement.

**Q: Is the Foundation Course free?**

Yes. The Foundation Course is free, and FDE provides a free book to registered groups. In Singapore the Foundations Group sessions are free too.

**Q: How long does the Foundation Course take?**

Eight sessions of about an hour to two hours each. Most groups meet weekly for eight weeks. Faith Driven Singapore meets monthly, so a cohort takes about eight months.

**Q: Who teaches the Foundation Course?**

The course content comes from Henry Kaestner, J.D. Greear and Chip Ingram. In the standard edition, J.D. Greear teaches each session and Henry Kaestner introduces it.

## Sources

- [FDE — Foundation Course](https://faithdrivenentrepreneur.org/foundation-course/)

- [FDE Participant Guide (PDF)](https://faithdrivenentrepreneur.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/FaithDrivenEntrepreneurParticipantGuide062022.pdf)

- [Faith Driven Singapore on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCy0L7vhcU5iSuap8kEmpHlA)

# What 22 sessions taught us: 7 insights from Singapore's faith-driven founders

URL: https://faithdriven.sg/articles/what-singapore-founders-say/
Published: 2026-09-24 · Category: Insights

We recorded, transcribed and coded two years of Faith Driven Singapore conversations. Here is what the data says Christ-following founders in Singapore care about.

## Quick answer

Across **22 recorded Foundations sessions** (August 2024 to August 2026, three cohorts, about 36 hours), Faith Driven Singapore coded **776 live sharings**. Seven patterns stand out: (1) calling is the core theme; (2) founders care about **hearing God** far more than about prosperity; (3) the **unicorn myth** drives burnout; (4) faith rewrites Asian scripts about **shame and money**; (5) witness in a multi-faith city is **character-first**; (6) the room is **ecumenical in practice**; (7) a **mobile, neutral community** keeps people coming back.

## How we did it

Every recorded session on our YouTube channel was transcribed the same way. Each live sharing was coded by question, theme (from a fixed list of 20) and signal, then checked back against its transcript. Curriculum films were excluded, and the facilitator's voice was kept separate, leaving **550 participant sharings**. Participants came from **at least 16 countries**.

## 1. Calling is the centre of gravity

**Calling and vocation** is the most common theme: 187 of 550 participant sharings, about one in three. Founders keep coming back to why they build. A digital-studio founder described feeling "looked down upon" in Singapore for not taking a corporate job, until "Jesus showed up in my life: I created you for a reason."

## 2. Discernment, not prosperity

**Spirit guidance and prayer** comes second (127 sharings). Explicit **prosperity** talk appears only 19 times, and pushback against it slightly outnumbers support (11 to 9). The distinctly charismatic thread in these rooms isn't "God will make you rich". It is **"God will tell you what to do"**: "Holy Spirit is my partner in this business… till You speak I will not do anything." ([watch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jeSK7lAcBAU&t=5234s))

Some participants also asked honestly how you hear God. "In times of confusion it is hard to discern," one said, and suggested "we could have a class on that".

## 3. The unicorn myth is a mental-health issue

**Identity and success** (105) and **suffering and mental health** (79) rank high. A former venture investor described depression and burnout driven by VCs demanding "100x or at least 10x". A mentor of 17 years observed that "if you're absolutely completely normal you wouldn't be an entrepreneur… we're more vulnerable people." The counterweight in the room was theological: "God is no less God because my business has cratered." See [Don't worship work](https://faithdriven.sg/articles/dont-worship-work-burnout-sabbath/).

## 4. Faith rewrites Asian success scripts

A quarter of all sharings (193 of 776) draw on a cultural script. The pattern is **selective**:

- Critiqued every time: shame about failure. "Everybody thinks that to be a leader you must be the smartest, the strongest. It's actually not true. A leader must be authentic, vulnerable."

- Mostly critiqued: Western hustle and VC culture, and the Chinese-family script that "money is the most important thing".

- Negotiated: religious plurality at work.

- Appreciated: Singapore's order, safety and just systems.

## 5. Witness in a multi-faith city is character-first

Most participants favoured **earning the right to speak**. They pray for a non-Christian client "as an outflow of doing things well", tell Bible stories to Muslim colleagues while knowing "I cannot go deeper", and hope people ask, "why are you like this? How come you have so much hope?" This is the Singapore version of FDE's Ministry in Word.

## 6. Ecumenical in practice

The room includes people from City Harvest, New Creation, Kingdomcity, Methodist and Lutheran churches, Catholics, house churches, two self-identified Orthodox Christians, and seekers who "haven't chosen my religion yet". Participants' language mixes evangelical, charismatic, Catholic social-teaching and Orthodox emphases, such as serving the common good, letting go of success, and treating brokenness as grace. It is ecumenism built on shared practice rather than on formal dialogue.

## 7. A mobile community keeps people

The group met in **seven venues in two years**, all within about 15 km of each other, and 23 of 24 sessions were in Singapore's Central Region. Even so, **47 people came back**, 24 followed the group to more than one venue, and 16 crossed from one cohort to the next. Because Singapore is small, moving is cheap. Neutral venues, which belong to no single church, suit a room drawn from many churches. And founders say they need each other: "Entrepreneurs struggle a lot… that's why the community is very important."

## What this means if you're a founder in Singapore

- You are not strange for asking what God thinks about your business. It's the most common question in the room.

- You're not alone in the burnout, the shame or the money pressure.

- There is a room where you can talk about all of it without anyone selling to you. [Come to the next gathering.](https://share.somin.ai/event-fde)

Read the quotes in full, with links to each moment in the recordings: [voices from the room](https://faithdriven.sg/voices/).

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: What do Christian entrepreneurs in Singapore care about most?**

In Faith Driven Singapore's coded sessions, the most common themes are calling and vocation, hearing God in decisions, stewardship of wealth, identity apart from success, and ethics and excellence.

**Q: Is the prosperity gospel common among Singapore's faith-driven founders?**

Not in these groups. Prosperity language appeared in 19 of 550 participant sharings, and pushback against it slightly outnumbered support.

**Q: How was this data collected?**

From 22 recorded Faith Driven Singapore Foundations sessions (2024–2026), transcribed with speech recognition, coded by theme and verified against the transcripts. Facilitator speech and curriculum films were separated out.

## Sources

- [Faith Driven Singapore recordings on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCy0L7vhcU5iSuap8kEmpHlA)

- Faith Driven Singapore, Foundations Voices research explorer (internal coding of 22 sessions, 2024–2026)
